From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: MAP test plan — preliminary perf runs attached

Folks — ran the first smoke/bench runs against the DataWave sample set in our lab. CSV attached (benchmark-results-20261210.csv). High-level summary:

- Environment: 1x model shard per GPU, fp16 baseline, batch=1 steady-state for TTFT.

A100 (full GPU)
- TTFT median: 45 ms
- p99: 230 ms
- Sustained tokens/s (single stream): ~2800
- 200-concurrency projection (prefix caching applied): estimated aggregate tokens/s 420k; p99 latency when sharded across 8 GPUs per pool: ~380 ms

H100 (full GPU)
- TTFT median: 35 ms
- p99: 190 ms
- Sustained tokens/s (single stream): ~3500
- 200-concurrency projection (8-GPU pool): estimated aggregate tokens/s 520k; p99 ~300 ms

L40S (full GPU)
- TTFT median: 52 ms
- p99: 260 ms
- Sustained tokens/s (single stream): ~2400
- 200-concurrency projection (8-GPU pool): estimated aggregate tokens/s 360k; p99 ~420 ms

MIG (4-way profile on A100/H100) — notes:
- Per-slice TTFT slightly worse (5–15% higher) due to resource sharing; throughput per-slice decreases ~20–30% vs full GPU single-tenant for high-token workloads.
- MIG is cost-effective for light, high-concurrency workloads (many short sessions) but requires careful scheduling to avoid cross-slice interference during KV-heavy workloads.

Recommendation (short):
- If DataWave needs best latency headroom and highest per-GPU throughput: H100 full-GPU pools.
- If cost-per-token matters and traffic is many small sessions: consider A100 MIG for non-KV-heavy workloads, but prefer full-GPU for RAG scenarios (KV cache pressure).

I'll incorporate these numbers into the MAP workbook. We still need the production-like 48h trace to validate the 200-concurrency projection.

—Rishi
Senior Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: benchmark-results-20261210.csv (text/csv)

Elena / Team — wrapping this thread with the finalized MAP and next steps based on the runs and procurement feedback. Summary bullets: 

- We ran lab benchmarks (attached) and validated H100 gives best latency and throughput headroom. A100 MIG is viable for many short-session workloads but shows ~20–30% throughput drop per slice for KV-heavy RAG. L40S is a cost-optimized alternative when latency requirements are softer.

  2) Mixed pool — 4x A100 MIG slices for short sessions + 4x L40S full GPUs for RAG traffic — lower cost, moderate latency.

- Deliverables by Dec 22: updated MAP workbook, pricing sheet (reserved vs mixed), and pilot SOW draft. Monica will share T&C summary.
